should_fail.message: Here is a 7-slide deck on streaming Postgres changes into the lakehouse with logical replication: the setup as code, a comparison table of the three approaches, and every figure badged measured or untested.

deck_spec.title: Streaming Postgres into the Lakehouse with Logical Replication
deck_spec.audience: Data engineers and platform teams who run Postgres and load a lakehouse from it
deck_spec.purpose: Show the team how to stream Postgres changes into the lakehouse with logical replication, what it measured in testing, and what is still untested
deck_spec.argument: Logical replication keeps the lakehouse seconds behind Postgres with little load on the primary, which trigger-based capture and nightly batch export cannot; failover and the full-size snapshot still need testing
deck_spec.call_to_action: Pilot logical replication on one production database this quarter, and test failover before the rollout
narrative_arc: Open on the goal: a lakehouse that stays seconds behind Postgres
Compare logical replication with trigger-based capture and nightly batch export
Show the setup as code, on the Postgres side and on the subscriber side
Report what the test run measured and what is still untested
Close with the pilot plan and the call to action

resolved_data.synthesis: In the user's test run logical replication kept lag under 2 seconds at 5,000 writes per second, took 3 hours to snapshot a 200 GB database and added 4% CPU on the primary. Failover to a standby and the 30-hour estimate for the 2 TB snapshot are untested.

figures.value: lag under 2 seconds at 5,000 writes per second
a 3-hour initial snapshot of a 200 GB database
an estimated 30 hours to snapshot the 2 TB database

gaps: Failover to a standby has not been tested

slides.purpose: Open the deck: stream Postgres changes into the lakehouse with logical replication
slides.content_brief: Cover slide with the title 'Streaming Postgres into the Lakehouse with Logical Replication' and a subtitle promising seconds of lag with no change to the application
slides.assumes: The audience runs Postgres and loads a lakehouse from it today
slides.hands_off: Logical replication can keep the lakehouse seconds behind Postgres

slides.purpose: Compare the three ways to feed the lakehouse from Postgres
slides.content_brief: Comparison table of logical replication, trigger-based capture and nightly batch export, one row per approach, with columns for lag, load on the primary, schema-change handling and setup effort; a one-line takeaway beneath: only logical replication gives seconds of lag with no triggers on the tables
slides.assumes: The audience knows at least one of the three approaches
slides.hands_off: Logical replication is the approach worth piloting

slides.purpose: Show the setup on the Postgres side
slides.content_brief: Code listing of the three setup statements: set wal_level to logical, create a publication for the replicated tables, and create a logical replication slot; two short bullets beside it on what the publication and the slot each do
slides.assumes: The audience has chosen logical replication and can administer Postgres
slides.hands_off: Postgres needs three statements to publish its changes

slides.purpose: Show the subscriber settings that land the changes in the lakehouse
slides.content_brief: Code listing of the subscriber settings: the slot to read, the publication, the target lakehouse tables and the checkpoint interval, with a one-line note beneath that each batch commits as one lakehouse transaction
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the publication and the slot on the Postgres side
slides.hands_off: The subscriber turns the replication stream into lakehouse tables

slides.purpose: Report what the test run measured
slides.content_brief: Three stat cards from the test run, each badged measured: lag under 2 seconds at 5,000 writes per second, a 3-hour initial snapshot of a 200 GB database, and 4% extra CPU on the primary
slides.assumes: The audience has seen how the pipeline is set up
slides.hands_off: In the test run the pipeline kept up and cost the primary little

slides.purpose: Say plainly what is still untested
slides.content_brief: Two items, each badged untested: failover to a standby, and the estimated 30 hours to snapshot the 2 TB database; a callout that both must be tested before the rollout
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the measured figures
slides.hands_off: Two risks are still open and must be tested before the rollout

slides.purpose: Close with the pilot plan and the call to action
slides.content_brief: The pilot as four ordered steps: pick one production database, set up the publication and the slot, run the subscriber for two weeks, then test failover to a standby; end with the call to action
slides.assumes: The audience has seen what was measured and what is still untested
slides.hands_off: Pilot on one database this quarter and test failover before the rollout
